chunks: And that which was narrated - Sa'd from Musa ibn al-Hasan and al-Hasan ibn Ali from Ahmad ibn Hilal and Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr and Umayyah ibn Ali al-Qaysi from Ali ibn Attiya from Zurara from one of them (peace be upon them): In

the Muhrim (person in Ihram), he said: 'He may cover his head and face when he intends to sleep.' This is to be understood as referring to one who fears harm from exposing it, in a state of non-choice. As for covering the face, this is permissible with choice, although it necessitates the Kaffarah (expiation). And whenever he does not intend the Kaffarah, it is not permissible for him to do so. That which indicates this is what was narrated:

key_terms.اَلْمُحْرِمُ: Person in the state of Ihram

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a Muhrim covering his face and head during sleep?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the juristic distinction between covering the head and face due to necessity (*darurah*) versus voluntary choice (*ikhtiyar*), a key debate in Shia fiqh regarding the validity of the pilgrimage. It establishes that voluntary face covering incurs an expiation (*kaffarah*) unless explicitly intended, reflecting the principle that minor violations of Ihram restrictions require compensation to maintain ritual purity.
